full_judgment: 10. Mr Md Abdullahel Baki, the learned Advocate appearing for the defendant-opposite party, on the other hand, opposes the Rule and supports the impugned judgment and decree, which was according to him just, correct and proper. The learned Advocate submits that the property as related in the decrees passed in Other Class Suit No. 476 of 1983 and 479 of 1983 are not at all related with the property of the present suit and therefore, the said decrees cannot stand in the way of well-founded judgment of the Court of appeal below. The learned Advocate further submits that in this case the plaintiff could not adduce any specific or clear evidence as to their possession in the suit land. Besides, the suit land as described in the schedule of the plaint is totally and thoroughly unspecified. Besides, in the facts and circumstances of the case the instant suit for permanent injunction is not maintainable as the property in question is an ancestral property of the defendants. The learned Advocate further submits that the plaintiff has not taken any attempt towards proving their title or possession in the suit land, plaintiff has neither exhibited CS khatian nor the kabuliyat of permanent settlement No. 12731/78 and 13734/78, the PW I admitted that “কবুলিয়ত নামাগুলো দাখিল করি নাই।” As such, the plaintiff -petitioner has miserably failed to prove their title and possession. He adds that the remedy in a suit for permanent injunction being an equitable one and that the plaintiff must come with clean hands, here the plaintiff's vendors, very tactfully, filed Other Class Suit No, 476/83 and 479/83 praying for declaration of title in shabek plot No. 457 and after obtaining ex-parte decree amended the schedule and entered the schedule of the defendant's property without notifying the defendants, the plaintiff being out of possession filed this suit for permanent injunction as a test case to enter into possession of the suit land and, as such, the plaintiff has not come with clean hands and hence is not entitled to get an equitable relief, as prayed for.
